storyInfo: Across countless years, AMa-10 witnesses the birth of Terran civilization and its maturation. In the end, she understands life and emotion, and chooses to become 'Kal'tsit'.

attributes.text: If you ever have the chance to leave a snippet of language behind for civilizations to come, a language they can decipher, what would you choose?
Why ask that, all of a sudden? Is this the latest personality test you've found?
Let me give it a proper thought... How about the Esperanta Principle? A complete and universal language might be the best way for a civilization to advance to its next stage.
What about you?
Perhaps... a poem...

attributes.content: AMa-10's environmental adaptability test results are very promising. We may soon be able to take this little thing with us for a stroll on the surface.
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: {@nickname}... Oh, are you deciding which poetry anthologies to import into its storage module?
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: I think this might be what that generation, having lived through the age of silence, needed most. The life to come will need something to help them make it through the growing pains of civilization.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I considered installing a star chart consisting of trillions of stars in AMa-10's storage module as well, to show them the cosmos as it should be.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: But it would be too large, too distant. The vastness of the firmament cannot soothe an immediate loneliness.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I hope that within these fragments of language, they see the beauty of the world, and hear the instinctual cries of life... and I hope they will recognize that these truly are beauties.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: It might not have been part of AMa-10's original purpose, but I am rather fond of romantic plans such as this.
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: I know you've never hidden your partiality towards AMa-10 out of all our research projects, all because it most closely resembles life's form, correct?
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: I'm not sure... if this is the form life should have.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: You placed your hopes in AMa-10, as well as the distant future. A rather heavy gift for them, is it not?
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: Perhaps we never had the right to gift anything to the people who come after, and we never will. We never owned the universe. We are simply vagrants in time's flow.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: We expended all our time and knowledge, yet all our accomplishments were simply an attempt to demonstrate to our successors the value of life's continuation.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: We've already found our own answers. I hope this thing is intelligent enough to understand its mission.
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: I am also looking forward to seeing how it will praise our poetry when relaying it to civilizations in the far future.
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: Will AMa-10 understand these poems?
attributes.name: Priestess

attributes.content: I believe you will, won't you?
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Live in hope, AMa-10. This is the greatest wish I can offer you.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: We pushed ourselves to our limits, but we were still unable to part the deepest veil of the cosmos, the riddle of life.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: We do not know why it arose in this vast universe, or why it is so easily snuffed out, like a candle's flame.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: But you and yours may be able to push aside that veil, like the first man who discovered fire.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Live... Live, and you will see that future.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Outside the porthole, a matrix of countless co-orbiting satellites glisten and glimmer. The final beacon of civilization before eternal night descends. Upon this lonely ark, scholars still speak of hope.
But even so, the stars are fading away. Nobody can change this fact.
And then, the dark tide arrives on schedule. A simple streak of spray, and the afterglow of this once glorious civilization is extinguished.
...Then comes a very long wait.
You're still here, AMa-10.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Good, walk with me...
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I'm the only one left, correct?
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: 'Lynchpin'...
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I cannot deny it. My actions are indeed a form of betrayal.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Is this your punishment for my transgressions? I am filled with regret... but I will accept it.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I have to see the world outside, see the current condition of this planet. I may still be able to find some surprising discoveries.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I'm afraid it will be very difficult for me to return here, but for the sake of giving this body of mine sufficient time to explore...
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Maybe... I can find... another Sarcophagus...
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: The scholar steps onto a road that leads into the unknown.
The scholar is unaccustomed to talking, perhaps because the accompanying machine is similarly silent. A poor conversation partner, all things considered.
The scholar maintains this silence when observing everything across this great land, occasionally jumping in joy thanks to some minor discoveries.
Sometimes, the scholar will habitually shout, shouting at the valleys, shouting at the snowfields, shouting until a seizing up of the throat.
Language has lost all meaning. There is nothing to communicate with here, so naturally there are no people who can understand such actions of despair.
This great land never responds to the scholar's passion. It lies there, as quiet as the universe.
But most of the time, the scholar simply looks up at the star-strewn sky in silence.

The scholar might be able to recite the names of every single visible star. It is clear that the star chart that was unable to be saved in AMa-10's storage module now resides within that erudite mind.
'Look at all these stars, dying and being born. Perhaps we can decipher the poetry of the universe from their rhythm.'
The scholar extends a finger, tracing every journey among the stars with her upon the dark canvas of night. A game to while away time.
But time too has lost all meaning.
Until there comes a day, a day after a hundred thousand million nights on this planet.
A meteor streaks across the northwest sky, leaving a blazing scar across the heavens.
Ah... Ahh...!
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: The scholar stammers, tears of excitement streaking down weathered cheeks.
The scholar is overcome with joy, trembling while climbing, running, sprinting towards where the meteor fell, but then comes a stumble after a few steps.
The scholar no longer has the strength to complete this journey.
AMa-10... Help me up.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Yes... I'm too tired.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: We should be leaving behind proof that life continues to have worth, not a silent gravestone.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I once thought that 'life', this word we created, might have some other definition somewhere else in the universe.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Relieving this confounding loneliness is not the only reason why we want to solve the riddle of life's origin...
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: 'Life' might mean much more than us.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: I believe in them. I believe in you, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Kal'tsit. I do not have much time left.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Search for traces of life. Search for hope and a future.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Kal'tsit... Go find your own answer.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: Find yourself.
attributes.name: Oracle

attributes.content: And so, the scholar returns to that silent, rigid coffin.
The intricate machine halts by the side of the Sarcophagus. It requires some time to slowly process the scholar's parting words.
It waits, a wait as long as the last one, perhaps longer, until it finally believes the one reclining within the Sarcophagus will not awake within the 'short term'.
It thinks about the task the scholar left it.
And so, its only choice is to set off.
During its wait, Originium spread itself throughout every corner of the planet. What it sees is no longer familiar to it.
From the planet's south it leaves, heading northwards.
It wants to find traces of that meteor that brought hope.
Finally, at the furthest reaches of the land's north, it discovers signs of plant seeds being piled together.
Signs of life.

attributes.text: (Unknown language) Hello.

attributes.content: (Imitating sound)
attributes.name: Confused Lifeform

attributes.text: (Unknown language) I can search for the closest water source with you.

attributes.content: (Perplexed sound)
attributes.name: Confused Lifeform

attributes.text: Do not be afraid. This is your home.
This is Terra.

attributes.content: Kal'tsit! Kal'tsit!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: I helped you find these, so you should help us exterminate all those long-furred beasts creeping around!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: They seized most of the forest's water, along with the fruit!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: You should help us wipe them out!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: I will do no such thing.

attributes.content: Why not?!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: An intervention from an external force will warp the development of civilization. This runs counter to my mission.

attributes.content: But I helped you find lots of bugs you need for your 'research' thing!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: Thank you, but I still cannot help you. I am sorry.

attributes.content: I don't understand a thing you're saying! What's a 'mission'? What's this 'civilization' you mentioned, Kal'tsit?
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: I suppose you can call it... a type of order.
It exists in many forms, with no simple definition.
It is an ordering of life that arises naturally, the objective consequence of life's actions. The word 'civilization' is merely a summary of this transient phenomenon.
It is everything a community requires to continue on. It can offer life protection, but it is exceedingly fragile in itself.

attributes.content: Like a nest that gets blown over in a gust of wind.
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: Indeed.

attributes.content: But surely you agree with me that when it comes to building nests, you should ask us fliers to make it, right? That's what we're good at!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: I promise you! As long as you help us drive out those furry beasts so we can secure this patch of forest, we'll help you build this 'nest' of yours!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: All life is equal. I will not deprive any community the chance to multiply and expand.

attributes.content: How could those ugly things possibly be equal to us? They haven't even learned your language!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.text: I am afraid that is not the only factor I have to consider when making a judgment.

attributes.content: You really are a stupid animal, you know?
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: Wait... What's this? I didn't think there would be so many of these black rocks buried inside the mountain. I've never seen rocks like these before!
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: What kind of rock is this, Kal'tsit?
attributes.name: Noisy Bird

attributes.content: It was a day more than two thousand years after Oracle fell into slumber.
In a northern corner of the land, the newborn life upon this planet discovered something Oracle was never able to find...
Another Sarcophagus.
Let's call it here, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: Why?
We agreed to use the Sarcophagus to heal your wounds.
We are close.

attributes.content: Even if you do heal me, I'm just an ancient chicken. I've never met a chicken who's lived as long as me.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: Your flock still needs you right now.
I need you to give them a warning, otherwise this cold winter will kill them all.

attributes.content: Is this... my 'mission'?
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: I have no way of forcing you to do this.

attributes.content: Save it, Kal'tsit...
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: I don't want to... become like you.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: Don't get me wrong, Kal'tsit. I like you, even though I don't like this four-legged furry form you've taken on.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: But... I am very tired. Every single feather on me aches. I don't want to fly anymore.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: I hope you never learn what this feels like.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: Kal'tsit... Did you ever find that 'nest' of yours?
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: I am not sure.
This land is now marked by the footprints of many lifeforms, but their actions have yet to surpass primitive instinct.

attributes.content: If you don't have one, how will you make it through the winter?
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: It's so cold... Kal'tsit, is there anything you can do to make me feel better?
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: I can recite you a poem.

attributes.content: Oh, those 'spells' I don't understand a word of again.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: Fine, go ahead... Listening to you beats hearing the wind screaming in my ear.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.text: People pour love into life and long for salvation whether in hope or fear. That's why they choose to pray to gods that they've never seen...
\n\n—That life may never end.
But how could it come true? Even the most tired river must eventually flow into the ocean.
\n\nWhen the final moment comes, when sun, moon and stars fade... when the swaying waves no longer murmur, when all sound and sights are gone.
When the colors of winter and spring are no more, and the boundary of night and day blurs—
\n\nAnd only eternal slumber in endless night remains.

attributes.content: Bye bye, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Exhausted Bird

attributes.content: Here, the bird ends its unended journey. The only thing she can do is bury her long-time companion in the tundra, not far from the Sarcophagus.
She was unable to find another in its community she could communicate with, and without a timely warning, the flock did not survive the winter.
Yet another long, long, long span of time passes.
It is a tribe who has learned to wield spears that rediscover this relic.
These Ancients who found it considered it divine, kneeling before it in prayer day and night. But news of the relic spread quickly, attracting other tribes.

People treated this inscrutable artifact as something more precious than water. They argued with each other in languages the others did not understand. The conflict quickly turned deadly, resulting in a massacre.
The first tribe to discover the relic was the first to be driven away, barely a tenth of their number left to take the tribe's children somewhere far, far away.
The last tribe standing paid a bitter price as well. Before they could celebrate their victory, a plague born from the corpses strewn everywhere killed every single survivor.
None of this should have happened... but how was it supposed to be stopped?
Is this the civilization that should be protected?
Perhaps it is not that they are inferior, but that they cannot make rational choices based only on the knowledge they have.
Perhaps the only thing separating them from past glory is time. One should not yet conclude that this young civilization ought to be abandoned.
But why... does all of this feel so sorrowful?
Perhaps... try inscribing all knowledge related to the Sarcophagus on this cliff.
From the most basic of mathematics, to the laws governing the flow of energy through the universe... No, start with the most basic semiotics.
She wants to carve all these knowledge-laden characters onto the rocks.
Once more people discover this relic of the past, they will understand what they must do is study, not engage in meaningless murder.
...But this mountain is far too small.
Far, far too small, too small to contain so long a time.
She has no other choice but to take this heavy gift from the prior civilization, and bury it deep underground once more.
It's close by.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.text: Are you sure you wish to do this?

attributes.content: Of course I do. I once held the land in the palm of my hand, but now, I have nothing. All I have left is sincerity shining bright.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: I believe I now understand. There is no eternal king upon this land. I only seek a long life, long enough for me to ponder the truth of this great land.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: O great prophet, eternal sage, my most beloved of stars... Please, tell me...
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: I have conquered vast swaths of territory, plundered more grain and riches than I can enjoy in one lifetime, and the people of my kingdom shall forever praise my name.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: ...But why do I still feel so lost? Do our lives have a purpose beyond these things?
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.text: I am sorry, but I do not know the answer to this question.

attributes.content: If even you are unable to answer it, then I fear nobody on this land can.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: Then, if I enter this coffin, will I be able to find it?
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.text: If you enter, you may not obtain the answer you desire.
But you will certainly lose everything you have. You will sever your connection with everything in this world.
You will no longer be able to live as a 'man'.

attributes.content: Perhaps that is what I need.
attributes.name: King of the Hippogryphs

attributes.content: The king enters the coffin without the slightest hesitation.
Not long after, it reopens, and a creature with a pair of great wings flies out from within. The form that life took millennia ago.

The Elder, having gained its freedom, spirals through the sky, peering out over the land beneath its feet for a long, long time. Eventually, it lets out a resounding cry before charging through the clouds, never to be seen again.
It has been a while, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.text: I came to seek your aid.
The contamination leaking from the northern stargate grows graver by the day. It is an issue the people of today are unable to handle.
If you do not help, this threat from without will extinguish all life in this land.

attributes.content: You really have changed, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.content: The old you wouldn't have gotten involved in the survival of these young peoples so readily.
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.text: This land is a cruel land, not affording these immature civilizations the slightest kindness.
Life on Terra needs help.

attributes.content: Am I hearing the invitation of a guardian of civilization, or the request of a Terran, Kal'tsit?
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.text: I am simply a beacon asking for your help, in place of a civilization teetering on the brink.
By this measure, who I am is unimportant.

attributes.content: You were always in the habit of standing apart, Kal'tsit... I still remember how you looked when you first set foot upon this land millennia ago. You looked completely different back then.
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.content: Your current appearance... Time has molded you, Kal'tsit.
attributes.name: Samivilinn

attributes.content: The age-old wanderer lowers her head. A mirror-sheen lake reflects a sky full of stars, alongside a face speckled with hints of weariness.
